newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia approves $6 bln rgt in highway projects.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia approves $6 bln rgt in highway projects.

text.p: Malaysia has approved three highway projects valued at a total of about 6.0 billion ringgit ($2.3 billion), Works Minister S. Samy Vellu was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency on Wednesday.
The three projects, to be constructed over a period of 15 years, were approved by the government at its weekly cabinet meeting on Wednesday, the minister said.
The first of them, a 22 km (13.6 mile) highway within Kuala Lumpur will be completed by 2001, Samy Vellu said.
It will be built by Medang Permai Sdn Bhd.
The company will collect tolls to recover its investment, Samy Vellu said.
He said the company has asked the government to provide an interest-free loan of 300 million ringgit and another soft loan of 350 million ringgit.
"If the government doesn't give this, the toll rate will be higher. The government has to spend a lot of money to provide this (facility)," Samy Vellu said.

He said another highway running through the suburbs of Kuala Lumpur would be built by Alloy Consolidated while the third, along the west coast of Malaysia, would be built by Konsortium Alam Ria. ($1 = 2.63 ringgit)
